newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil, Kaliningrad region sign co-operation deal.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil, Kaliningrad region sign co-operation deal.

text.p: Russia's leading oil company LUKoil on Wednesday signed a wide-ranging cooperation deal with the Kaliningrad enclave on the Baltic Sea to develop oil projects for regional and export markets.

LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov told reporters that the broad agreement with Russia's Kaliningrad Region covered oil production, sales of crude oil and oil products in the area, crude oil sales in Western markets and offshore oil equipment production.

"Kaliningrad oil is exceptionally light, and to refine it around here when there are no big export outlets would not make sense," Alekperov told reporters after a signing ceremony. "It's more profitable to refine in Western markets, like in Poland."
The two sides also agreed to conduct seismic studies of on- and offshore hydrocarbon reserves in the Kravtsovskoye area of the Baltic Sea shelf.
LUKoil also plans a refined oil products loading terminal in the region's Izhevskoye area, but LUKoil officials said plans had not been finalised.
Alekperov said LUKoil had no plans to build refineries in Kaliningrad, a small region wedged between Lithuania and Poland near Belarus and is not linked by land to Moscow.
It is Russia's western-most region but has no oil pipelines.
Alekperov also said LUKoil had no plans to join forces with Western companies eyeing Baltic shelf reserves.
"We plan working in this area only within the framework of Kaliningradmorneft (a LUKoil subsidiary formerly known as Kaliningradmorneftegaz)," he said.
LUKoil, Russia's largest oil producer, also opened two retail gasoline outlets in and around Kaliningrad, bringing its total number of outlets in the region to four.
It opened its first gasoline station in Warsaw in August, and supplies it with Kaliningrad oil refined at four small refineries owned by state-run Nafta Polska SA in southeastern Poland.

Kaliningrad regional administration officials said Russia's Surgutneftegaz, which owns a network of formerly-state owned gasoline stations in the area but has not invested significantly in them, was losing ground to LUKoil.
LUKoil-Kaliningradmorneft has estimated on- and offshore oil reserves of up to 60 million tonnes and produced over 742,000 tonnes of crude last year.
